canonical_names: The canonical spelling is the name printed and the name a page is titled with, so it is the player's real name rather than whichever spelling the data happens to use most. Suffixes are written the way the rest of the data writes them, with no full stop. The alias keys are the raw spellings in data.json and never change: they are what matches.

readme: Two spellings of one player, merged into one identity for the engine. Read by scripts/factoids.py and reusable by the prerender script; build_data.py and data.json are untouched. Without this, each half looks like a separate short career: the older spelling looks finished and the newer one starts mid-career with the other half's running total already on it. Candidate rule and evidence below; the canonical spelling is the one the data uses most, and on a tie the one carrying the most recent season.
rule: Names that match once Jr / Sr / II / III / IV / V, full stops and apostrophes are stripped, with the same draft year (or one missing), no season in common, and seasons that run continuously together (no gap longer than 1 season). A shared season means two men; a hole in the run is a career gap, which data/identity_splits.json handles instead.
